flushPolicy.note: theoreticalMaxGroupCommitPerSec = serial.fsyncsPerSec × batchMax (full batches). Parallel must not be used as this ceiling.

serial.pattern: one writer; write(batchMax NDJSON lines); fsyncSync; wait; repeat — matches trigger-journal group_commit

serialGrowingLong.pattern: Same as serial_board_matched but longer wall time so the file grows like a board focus window — tests metadata cost of a growing journal.
serialGrowingLong.note: Compare fsyncLatencyMs.p50/p99 to serial_board_matched; a 2–4× rise supports the growing-metadata hypothesis.

serialFdatasync.pattern: one writer; append batch; fdatasyncSync (data only — skips unused metadata)
serialFdatasync.note: Experimental arm — report before/after fsyncsPerSec + latency vs serial_board_matched.

serialPreallocFdatasync.pattern: fallocate segment; positioned writes within allocated size; fdatasync — size/blocks stable across syncs
serialPreallocFdatasync.note: Experimental arm — if this closes most of the board-vs-probe gap, campaign should use the same sync path.

parallel.pattern: 8 fio jobs; each write+fsync; aggregate IOPS — NOT the group_commit ceiling

overwriteDiagnostic.note: Not the board pattern — kept only to explain prior inflated probes that rewrote one offset.

armsCompare.hypothesis: Appending log + fsync forces size/allocation metadata each sync; long growing runs and board focus windows may show higher latency than a short probe. fdatasync + preallocated segments are the standard fix — report before/after sustained rate and fsyncs/sec.

reading.verdict: Serial single-writer fsyncs/sec still far above ~4k. Board rates well below theoreticalMaxGroupCommitPerSec need under-load sync latency vs this probe — growing-file metadata is the leading suspect when producer CPU is idle.
reading.action: Compare flushStats.fsyncLatencyMs.p50/p99 to serial.fsyncLatencyMs. If run latency is 2–4× the probe, try fdatasync + preallocate arms on both systems before the campaign.
reading.bothSystems: Ontologiql must run the same serial_board_matched probe (one writer, one sync in flight, batch-then-fsync) on the shared host before claiming disk-bound. Both sides should also compare under-load sync latency to the probe and trial fdatasync+prealloc if latency is inflated.
reading.priorMistake: An earlier probe that looked like ~40k fsync/s was overwrite-same-offset / parallel-capable and overstated single-writer capacity. Retracted as the group_commit ceiling.
